title: Cell Squeezing as a Robust, Microfluidic Intracellular Delivery Platform
protocol: Store the reservoirs, holders, O-rings, and microfluidic devices in 70% ethanol.
Use a container with a lid for each type of component (container 1 for devices, container 2 for reservoirs and O-rings, container 3 for holders).
Change the ethanol solution in containers 2 and 3 before each use to prevent cross-contamination.
Place containers 2 and 3 in an ultrasound bath for 5-10 minutes before each use.
Clean the workspace in the biosafety cabinet with a 70% ethanol solution.
Spray all materials (containers, tweezers) with a 70% ethanol solution before placing them inside the biosafety cabinet.
Set down 2-3 low-lint wipes in the work area for assembly.
Remove plastic reservoirs from container 2 using tweezers and place on wipes to allow evaporation of ethanol.
Gently tap the reservoirs or blow air through them to facilitate removal of ethanol solution.
Insert O-rings into their appropriate slots on the reservoirs.
Remove holder and chips from respective containers and allow ethanol to evaporate (~1-2 min).
Use tweezers to place the desired chip face-up (i.e., access holes up) in the holder.
Raise the holder with the chip to eyelevel to ensure the chip is lying flat and adjust if necessary.
Gently place the reservoirs on the holder and align them with the clips.
Press down on the reservoirs until they click into place.
Ensure both sides of the reservoirs are secure and that the chip appears to be in the correct position.
Plate cells 1-2 days prior to the experiment such that they are no more than 80% confluent on the day of the experiment.
Place cells in suspension (in PBS or relevant media) aiming for an operating concentration of 1.0 x 10^6 cells/ml to 1.0 x 10^7 cells/ml.
Mix cells with the desired delivery material in a separate tube to obtain the desired concentration for the experiment.
Pipette the mixture of cells and delivery material into a reservoir (maximum capacity 150 μl).
Attach pressure tubing to the filled reservoir and tighten it securely (finger tight is often sufficient).
Adjust the pressure on the regulator to control the speed at which cells travel through the device.
Press the button to pressurize the reservoir and start cell flow.
Turn the regulator to 0 psi when the liquid level is approximately 2 mm from the bottom of the reservoir.
Collect treated cells from the appropriate reservoir and place them in the desired collection tube or plate.
Do not dilute collected cells at this stage as porated cells will continue to uptake material for up to 10 minutes.
Dilute the cells in the desired media or buffer after 10 minutes have passed.
Repeat steps 5.1 - 5.7 if more treated cells are needed or alternative experimental conditions are required.
Exchange chips as needed if they clog and discard any clogged devices.
Gently disconnect the reservoirs from the main holder by pushing aside the clip arms.
Place each part in the appropriate storage container.
Place used chips in a separate container for disposal.
